context: To get the time complexity, we assume that each edge is labelled with the time step at which it appears. Note that such a list can be computed by checking the set of active edges for each snapshot in the graph. As there are at most n − 1 edges, each of which are active for at most t time steps, this will take at most O(t · n) time. For each snapshot, at most k edges need to be checked for each vertex. Therefore, as there are at most k time steps at which each edge is active, the total complexity of this algorithm is O(n · k · t). ◀ Finally, we provide a lower boundpon the temporal harmonious chromatic number of the class of (k, t)-temporal matchings of 8(min(k, t) − 1). In doing so, we provide a clear gap between the upper and lower bounds and leave open the question of the optimal bound for (2, √ 2)-temporal matchings and (2, 3) temporal matchings.
